datasets.instrument_sensor: Mars Environmental Dynamics Analyzer (MEDA) instrument package; Relative Humidity Sensor (HS); Thermal Infrared Sensor (TIRS); Air Temperature Sensor (ATS); pressure sensor; PRT temperature sensors (during sealing)
datasets.measurement_observable: Near-surface relative humidity (with respect to ice) at 1.45 m; atmospheric pressure; air temperature; ground/surface brightness temperature; derived water vapor pressure, water vapor volume mixing ratio (VMR), precipitable water column estimate, and derived surface water activity (aw)
datasets.wavelength_bandpass: TIRS ground brightness temperature in 8–14 µm range
datasets.data_type_product_type: In-situ meteorology/environmental time series; derived parameters (VMR, aw)
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: First Martian year of Perseverance operations; examples include sols 285–305 (Ls=139°–149°) and water VMR peak near Ls=150°; sealing times span LMST 16:25 to 22:16 and sols listed in Table 1 (e.g., sol 120 through sol 639)
datasets.location_coverage: MEDA measurements at Jezero crater; HS/TIRS on rover mast ~1.5 m; HS/RH at 1.45 m; water activity derived using HS with TIRS ground temperature; Jezero latitudinal bin noted as 18°–21° N for comparison with TES
datasets.spatial_resolution: TIRS downward-looking channel covering an ellipsoid area of 3–4 m2
datasets.temporal_resolution_cadence: HS output reliable above 2% RH and used for local times ~20:00 to 07:00 (seasonally varying); ATS referenced with 300 s moving average; other cadence not stated
datasets.how_used: Primary in-situ dataset used to characterize Jezero near-surface water cycle and habitability metrics by deriving water vapor VMR, precipitable water, and surface water activity (aw) and relating these to temperature through diurnal/seasonal cycles and sample sealing conditions (Table 1, Figs. 2–4).

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Mars 2020 Initial Reports—Crater Floor Campaign (Volume 1) and Mars 2020 Initial Reports—Delta Front Campaign (Volume 2); Sample Dossier products
datasets.instrument_sensor: Perseverance rover instrument payload observations at sampling sites (not individually enumerated for dossier content in this paper); rover ancillary data
datasets.measurement_observable: Sampling acquisition details and instrument observation interpretation for each cached sample; observations from instrument payloads at sampling site with rover ancillary data
datasets.data_type_product_type: Sample Dossier; Initial Report (per-sample report product)
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: Samples 1 through 21 (first Martian year; Crater Floor Campaign ended on sol 380; Delta Front Campaign began on sol 415 and ended on sol 707)
datasets.location_coverage: Sampling sites along Perseverance traverse in Jezero crater including First Cache/Sample Depot at Three Forks
datasets.how_used: Used as the documented source for sampling acquisition details and instrument observation interpretation; also the source of the sample-related parameters and context referenced for the analysis (e.g., sealing sols and sampling details referenced as 'Initial Reports-PDS' and described in Methods).

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Thermal Emission Spectrometer (TES) water column abundance climatology dataset (non-normalized to constant surface pressure)
datasets.measurement_observable: Derived atmospheric water vapor column abundance (total column H2O)
datasets.data_type_product_type: Orbital climatology dataset; zonally averaged column abundance values
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: Mars Years 24–27; daytime observations with LMST ~14:00; values provided in Ls=5° averaged bins
datasets.location_coverage: TES climatology dataset given in 3° latitude, 7.5° longitude bins; Jezero comparison uses latitudinal bin 18°–21° N; data were zonally averaged
datasets.how_used: Used as the orbital reference for daytime, zonally averaged water vapor column abundance for the Jezero region and compared against MEDA pre-dawn in-situ estimates (Fig. 2 bottom).

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Thermal Emission Imaging System (THEMIS) atmosphere observations and Mars Climate Sounder (MCS) atmosphere observations used for Mars Year 36 airborne dust climatology
datasets.instrument_sensor: Thermal Emission Imaging System (THEMIS); Mars Climate Sounder (MCS)
datasets.measurement_observable: Observations of Martian atmosphere used to obtain climatology of airborne dust for year 36 and reconstruct simulated spatial and vertical dust distributions (dust scenario of MY36)
datasets.data_type_product_type: Orbital atmospheric observations (dust-related); dust climatology inputs for model reconstruction
datasets.location_coverage: Used to reconstruct simulated spatial and vertical dust distributions; model extraction performed at Jezero location (a box of 5°×5° in the GCM) at Ls=144°
datasets.how_used: Used to build the MY36 dust scenario/climatology that constrained the Mars Planetary Climate Model (PCM) simulations, which were then compared with MEDA water vapor variability and column water vapor at Jezero.

output_parsed.paper_title: Present-day thermal and water activity environment of the Mars Sample Return collection

queries.query: For Jezero Crater on Mars during the first Martian year of the Mars 2020 mission, I need the complete Perseverance MEDA in-situ meteorology record (relative humidity with respect to ice, surface pressure, mast air temperatures, and thermal-infrared ground brightness temperature) to quantify the seasonal/diurnal near-surface water cycle and identify periods consistent with transient frost conditions.

Using Perseverance MEDA observations at Jezero Crater, I want the mission-provided derived environmental parameters (including water vapor volume mixing ratio estimates and surface water activity derived from humidity and thermal-infrared ground temperature) to evaluate nighttime vs daytime habitability-relevant thresholds across the first Martian year, emphasizing local night when the humidity sensor measurements are most reliable.

final_output.query: For Jezero Crater on Mars during the first Martian year of the Mars 2020 mission, I need the complete Perseverance MEDA in-situ meteorology record (relative humidity with respect to ice, surface pressure, mast air temperatures, and thermal-infrared ground brightness temperature) to quantify the seasonal/diurnal near-surface water cycle and identify periods consistent with transient frost conditions.

Using Perseverance MEDA observations at Jezero Crater, I want the mission-provided derived environmental parameters (including water vapor volume mixing ratio estimates and surface water activity derived from humidity and thermal-infrared ground temperature) to evaluate nighttime vs daytime habitability-relevant thresholds across the first Martian year, emphasizing local night when the humidity sensor measurements are most reliable.

Assemble the complete Mars 2020 Perseverance returned-sample site documentation for Jezero crater during the first Martian year, including instrument payload observations collected at each sampling locality plus the associated rover ancillary context, to reconstruct sampling conditions and lithologic variability across the crater-floor and delta-front phases.

Compile the document-only archive of Mars 2020 Perseverance per-sample science team reports and consolidated sampling documentation for cached samples from Jezero crater sealed during the crater-floor through delta-front operations, to extract standardized metadata on sealing conditions, sampling sequence, and interpretive notes per tube.

Using Mars Global Surveyor Thermal Emission Spectrometer observations, I need the mission-long, derived-processing-level nadir atmospheric opacity time series on Mars to quantify seasonal atmospheric attenuation relevant to column water-vapor retrieval intercomparisons.

For Mars Global Surveyor Thermal Emission Spectrometer, compile derived infrared column aerosol optical depths (dust and water ice) for Mars Years 24–27 in solar-longitude bins to characterize seasonal variability for comparison with regional near-surface humidity measurements.

For Mars Year 36, I need Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter Mars Climate Sounder derived atmospheric profile products to constrain the vertical distribution of airborne dust for a Jezero-region dust climatology reconstruction (target: Mars; product type: derived data record / Level 2).

For Mars Year 36, I need Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter Mars Climate Sounder calibrated sensor-level measurements suitable for re-deriving dust opacity constraints used in airborne dust climatology inputs (target: Mars; product type: reduced data record / Level 1B).
